name: Coherent-one-way quantum key distribution over 250 km of ultra-low-loss fibre with NbN SSPDs at 2.5 K in a cryogen-free closed-cycle cryostat
plain_name: Send secret quantum encryption keys over 250 km of optical fibre using cold superconducting detectors
description: Stucki et al. (Geneva/Corning) run a 625 MHz COW QKD prototype over 250 km of SMF-28 ULL fibre; Bob uses two fibre-coupled NbN meander SSPDs at 2.5 K in a cryogen-free pulse-tube cryostat, biased at 26.5 uA for 2.65% efficiency at a 5 Hz dark-count rate.
keywords: Send secret quantum encryption keys over 250 km of optical fibre using cold superconducting detectors

sources.citation: High rate, long-distance quantum key distribution over 250km of ultra low loss fibres (Stucki et al., arXiv:0903.3907, New J. Phys. 2009)

requirements.rationale: The detector efficiency/dark-count trade-off used for the 250 km key exchange was characterised and operated at 2.5 K.
Two SSPDs (data line and monitoring line) must be current-biased and read out electrically.
Optional: the prototype deliberately used a cryogen-free closed-cycle cryostat instead of liquid-helium cooling for practical field integration.

confirmation_note: Requirements taken from the cited procedure and independently re-verified against the source (research/v4, 2026-11-01). Users must confirm them for their own run; edits require confirmation again.
